visual_goal: Show the sourcing decision as a sequence of gates: differentiation, volume, controls burden, with every sourcing outcome passing through a final cost and exit check that can loop back to the start.
prompt: A left-to-right decision path. At the far left a starting signpost labeled 'Capability'. A road runs right through three arch gates in a row; each gate carries one label on its top bar: 'Advantage?', 'Volume?' and 'Controls?'. After the last gate the road splits into five parallel lanes stacked vertically, each lane passing one rounded sign: 'Build', 'Buy and extend', 'Compose', 'Fit-to-standard', 'Outsource'. The five lanes merge again into one road that enters a small booth with a lifting barrier; the booth roof carries the label 'Cost and exit'. From the booth one green arrow continues right to a document icon labeled 'Decision record'. One long orange arrow curves from the booth back along the top of the picture to the signpost 'Capability'.
alt: A road from a capability through gates for advantage, volume and controls, fanning out to build, buy and extend, compose, fit-to-standard and outsource, all merging into a cost and exit checkpoint that leads to a decision record or loops back to the start.

visual_goal: Show vendor selection as a series of gates where knock-outs, the proof of concept and the exit test can each exclude a vendor, and only survivors get a weighted score.
prompt: A left-to-right conveyor belt carrying small generic boxes past stations. At the far left a clipboard labeled 'Requirements', then a big pile of boxes labeled 'Longlist'. Next an arch gate labeled 'Knock-outs'. Next a screen labeled 'Demos' and a phone labeled 'References'. Next an arch gate labeled 'Proof of concept'. Next an arch gate labeled 'Exit test'. Next a handshake labeled 'Contract terms'. Next a balance scale labeled 'Weighted score', then a document labeled 'Decision record'. Fewer boxes ride the belt after each gate. Below the belt sits one bin labeled 'Excluded'. Exactly three red arrows go down into the bin, each starting directly at the foot of one arch gate: one from 'Knock-outs', one from 'Proof of concept', one from 'Exit test'.
alt: Vendor boxes passing from requirements and a longlist through knock-out, proof of concept and exit-test gates, each of which can drop vendors into an excluded bin, before contract terms, a weighted score and a decision record.

visual_goal: Show that every acquired finance system is wrapped first; it is kept as a tier only if business model differs, the platform fits and it becomes a reusable template, otherwise it converges or stays wrapped pending a carve-out.
prompt: A left-to-right illustration. At the far left a small generic server box labeled 'Acquired system'. One arrow into the same box now wrapped in a clear protective shell labeled 'Wrap'. From the wrapped box a path of arrows passes three small diamond checkpoints in a row: 'Different model?', 'Platform fits?', 'Reusable template?'. A green arrow from 'Reusable template?' leads right to a sturdy shelf labeled 'Keep as tier'. Below the first two diamonds sits a wide blue funnel labeled 'Converge' over a large building labeled 'Group core'. Exactly two arrows drop into the funnel: one from 'Different model?' and one from 'Platform fits?'. Below 'Reusable template?' sits a fourth diamond labeled 'Carve-out?' with one arrow down into it from 'Reusable template?'. From 'Carve-out?' one arrow goes right to a still-wrapped box labeled 'Keep wrapped' and one arrow goes left into the 'Converge' funnel.
alt: An acquired system is wrapped first, then passes checks for a different business model, platform fit and reusable template; it is kept as a tier only if all hold, otherwise it converges onto the group core or stays wrapped if a carve-out is likely.
